questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Jhelum River passes through Wular Lake.
2. Krishna River directly feeds Kolleru Lake.
3. Meandering of Gandak River formed Kanwar Lake.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Jhelum flows through Wular Lake. Kolleru is fed by the Budameru and Tammileru streams, not directly by the Krishna, and Kanwar Lake was formed by the Burhi Gandak. Only one is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q1

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs: Port Well known as
1. Kamarajar Port First major port in India registered as a company
2. Mundra Port Largest privately owned port in India
3. Visakhapatnam Port Largest container port in India
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Kamarajar (Ennore) was the first major port registered as a company, and Mundra is the largest private port. The largest container port is JNPT, not Visakhapatnam.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q2

questions.q:
Consider the following trees:
1. Jackfruit (Artocarpus heterophyllus)
2. Mahua (Madhuca indica)
3. Teak (Tectona grandis)
How many of the above are deciduous trees?
questions.e: Teak and mahua are deciduous trees of monsoon forests. Jackfruit is evergreen.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q3

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. India has more arable area than China.
2. The proportion of irrigated area is more in India as compared to China.
3. The average productivity per hectare in Indian agriculture is higher than that in China.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: India has more arable land than China, but China irrigates a larger share and gets higher yields per hectare. Only one is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q4

questions.q: Which one of the following is the best example of repeated falls in sea level, giving rise to present-day extensive marshland?
questions.e: The Rann of Kutch was once a shallow arm of the sea; repeated falls in sea level left a vast seasonal salt marsh.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q5

questions.q: Ilmenite and rutile, abundantly available in certain coastal tracts of India, are rich sources of which one of the following?
questions.e: Ilmenite and rutile from coastal beach sands are the main ores of titanium.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q6

questions.q: About three-fourths of world's cobalt, a metal required for the manufacture of batteries for electric motor vehicles, is produced by
o: the Democratic Republic of the Congo
questions.e: The Democratic Republic of the Congo produces about three-quarters of the world's mined cobalt.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q7

questions.q: Which one of the following is a part of the Congo Basin?
questions.e: South-eastern Cameroon lies in the Congo Basin forests. Nigeria drains to the Niger, and South Sudan and Uganda lie in the Nile basin.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q8

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Amarkantak Hills are at the confluence of Vindhya and Sahyadri Ranges.
2. Biligirirangan Hills constitute the easternmost part of Satpura Range.
3. Seshachalam Hills constitute the southernmost part of Western Ghats.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Amarkantak is where the Vindhya and Satpura (Maikal) ranges meet, Biligirirangan links the Eastern and Western Ghats, and Seshachalam is part of the Eastern Ghats. None is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q9

questions.q:
With reference to India's projects on connectivity, consider the following statements:
1. East-West Corridor under Golden Quadrilateral Project connects Dibrugarh and Surat.
2. Trilateral Highway connects Moreh in Manipur and Chiang Mai in Thailand via Myanmar.
3. Bangladesh-China-India-Myanmar Economic Corridor connects Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh with Kunming in China.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: The East-West Corridor runs Silchar to Porbandar, the Trilateral Highway Moreh to Mae Sot, and the BCIM corridor Kolkata to Kunming. None is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q10

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: India, despite having uranium deposits, depends on coal for most of its electricity production.
Statement-II: Uranium, enriched to the extent of at least 60%, is required for the production of electricity.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Coal produces most of India's electricity. Power reactors use natural or low-enriched uranium (under 5%), not 60%, so Statement-II is wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q11

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Marsupials are not naturally found in India.
Statement-II: Marsupials can thrive only in montane grasslands with no predators.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Marsupials are native to Australia, New Guinea and the Americas, not India. They live in many habitats, not only predator-free montane grasslands.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q12

questions.q: ‘Invasive Species Specialist Group’ (that develops Global Invasive Species Database) belongs to which one of the following organizations?
o: The International Union for Conservation of Nature
The United Nations World Commission for Environment and Development
The World Wide Fund for Nature
questions.e: The Invasive Species Specialist Group belongs to IUCN's Species Survival Commission and runs the Global Invasive Species Database.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q13

questions.q:
Consider the following fauna:
1. Lion-tailed Macaque
2. Malabar Civet
3. Sambar Deer
How many of the above are generally nocturnal or most active after sunset?
questions.e: The Malabar civet is nocturnal. The lion-tailed macaque is active by day, and UPSC's key does not count the sambar as mainly nocturnal. So only one.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q14

questions.q: Which of the following organisms perform waggle dance for others of their kin to indicate the direction and the distance to a source of their food?
questions.e: Honeybees perform the waggle dance to tell hive-mates the direction and distance of food.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q15

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Some mushrooms have medicinal properties.
2. Some mushrooms have psychoactive properties.
3. Some mushrooms have insecticidal properties.
4. Some mushrooms have bioluminescent properties.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Different mushrooms are medicinal, psychoactive, insecticidal or bioluminescent. All four are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q16

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian squirrels:
1. They build nests by making burrows in the ground.
2. They store their food materials like nuts and seeds in the ground.
3. They are omnivorous.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Indian palm squirrels nest in trees, not burrows. They store nuts and seeds in the ground and eat both plant and animal food.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q17

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Some microorganisms can grow in environments with temperature above the boiling point of water.
2. Some microorganisms can grow in environments with temperature below the freezing point of water.
3. Some microorganisms can grow in highly acidic environment with a pH below 3.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Extremophile microbes grow above 100°C, below freezing and below pH 3. All three are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q18

questions.q: Which one of the following makes a tool with a stick to scrape insects from a hole in a tree or a log of wood?
questions.e: Orangutans shape sticks into tools to extract insects and honey from holes.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q19

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Aerosols
2. Foam agents
3. Fire retardants
4. Lubricants In the making of how many of the above are hydrofluorocarbons used?
questions.e: HFCs are used as aerosol propellants, foam-blowing agents and fire suppressants, but not in lubricants.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q20

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Interest income from the deposits in Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) distributed to their investors is exempted from tax, but the dividend is taxable.
Statement-II: InvITs are recognized as borrowers under the ‘Securitization and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002’.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: InvIT interest is taxed in the investors' hands while dividends are generally exempt, so Statement-I is reversed. The Finance Act 2021 brought InvITs under SARFAESI as borrowers.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q21

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: In the post-pandemic recent past, many Central Banks worldwide had carried out interest rate hikes.
Statement-II: Central Banks generally assume that they have the ability to counteract the rising consumer prices via monetary policy means.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Central banks raised rates after the pandemic because they believe tighter money cools demand and inflation. Statement-II explains Statement-I.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q22

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Carbon markets are likely to be one of the most widespread tools in the fight against climate change.
Statement-II: Carbon markets transfer resources from the private sector to the State.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Carbon markets are spreading as a climate tool. Allowance auctions can move money to the State, but that is not their essential nature or the reason for their spread.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q23

questions.q: Which one of the following activities of the Reserve Bank of India is considered to be part of ‘sterilization’?
o: Oversight of settlement and payment systems
Debt and cash management for the Central and State Governments
Regulating the functions of Non-banking Financial Institutions
questions.e: Sterilisation offsets the money effect of RBI's forex operations, mainly through open market operations.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q24

questions.q:
Consider the following markets:
1. Government Bond Market
2. Call Money Market
3. Treasury Bill Market
4. Stock Market
How many of the above are included in capital markets?
questions.e: Capital markets deal in long-term funds: government bonds and shares. Call money and T-bills are money market instruments.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q25

questions.q: Which one of the following best describes the concept of ‘Small Farmer Large Field’?
o: Resettlement of a large number of people, uprooted from their countries due to war, by giving them a large cultivable land which they cultivate collectively and share the produce
Many marginal farmers in an area organize themselves into groups and synchronize and harmonize selected agricultural operations

Many marginal farmers in an area together, make a contract with a corporate body and surrender their land to the corporate body for a fixed term for which the corporate body makes a payment of agreed amount to the farmers

A company extends loans, technical knowledge and material inputs to a number of small farmers in an area so that they produce the agricultural commodity required by the company for its manufacturing process and commercial production
questions.e: Under 'Small Farmer Large Field', small farmers organise into groups and synchronise operations like sowing and spraying to get economies of scale.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q26

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Government of India provides Minimum Support Price for niger (Guizotia abyssinica) seeds.
2. Niger is cultivated as a Kharif crop.
3. Some tribal people in India use niger seed oil for cooking.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Niger seed has an MSP, is a kharif crop, and its oil is used for cooking by some tribal communities. All three are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q27

questions.q:
Consider the investments in the following assets:
1. Brand recognition
2. Inventory
3. Intellectual property
4. Mailing list of clients
How many of the above are considered intangible investments?
questions.e: Brands, intellectual property and client mailing lists are intangible. Inventory is a tangible asset.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q28

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Demographic performance
2. Forest and ecology
3. Governance reforms
4. Stable government
5. Tax and fiscal efforts For the horizontal tax devolution, the Fifteenth Finance Commission used how many of the above as criteria other than population area and income distance?
questions.e: Besides population, area and income distance, the 15th Finance Commission used forest and ecology, demographic performance and tax effort. That is three.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q29

questions.q:
Consider the following infrastructure sectors:
1. Affordable housing
2. Mass rapid transport
3. Health care
4. Renewable energy On how many of the above does UNOPS Sustainable Investments in Infrastructure and Innovation (S3i) initiative focus for its investments?
questions.e: UNOPS's S3i initiative focused on affordable housing, renewable energy and health care, not mass transit.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q30

questions.q: In essence, what does ‘Due Process of Law’ mean?
questions.e: 'Due process of law' lets courts test whether a law itself is fair and just; at its core is the principle of natural justice.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q31

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: In India, prisons are managed by State Governments with their own rules and regulations for the day-to-day administration of prisons.
Statement-II: In India, prisons are governed by the Prisons Act, 1894 which expressly kept the subject of prisons in the control of Provincial Governments.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Prisons are a State subject, so States run them with their own rules. The Prisons Act 1894 placed prisons under provincial governments, which explains Statement-I.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q32
questions.u: Justice Administration, Law Enforcement & Statutory Frameworks

questions.q: Which one of the following statements best reflects the Chief purpose of the ‘Constitution’ of a country?
o: It determines the objective for the making of necessary laws.
It enables the creation of political offices and a government.
It defines and limits the powers of government.
It secures social justice, social equality and social security.
questions.e: A constitution's chief purpose is to define and limit the powers of government.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q33

questions.q: In India, which one of the following Constitutional Amendments was widely believed to be enacted to overcome the judicial interpretations of the Fundamental Rights?
questions.e: UPSC dropped this question. The First Amendment (1951) was enacted to overcome court rulings on Fundamental Rights.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q34

questions.q:
Consider the following organizations/bodies in India:
1. The National Commission for Backward Classes
2. The National Human Rights Commission
3. The National Law Commission
4. The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
How many of the above are constitutional bodies?
questions.e: Only the NCBC is constitutional (Article 338B). The NHRC and NCDRC are statutory, and the Law Commission is set up by executive order.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q35

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. If the election of the President of India is declared void by the Supreme Court of India, all acts done by him/her in the performance of duties of his/her office of President before the date of decision become invalid.
2. Election for the post of the President of India can be postponed on the ground that some Legislative Assemblies have been dissolved and elections are yet to take place.
3. When a Bill is presented to the President of India, the Constitution prescribes time limits within which he/she has to declare his/her assent.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Acts of a President whose election is voided remain valid (Article 71), the election cannot be delayed for dissolved Assemblies, and there is no time limit for assent. None is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q36

questions.q:
With reference to Finance Bill and Money Bill in the Indian Parliament, consider the following statements:
1. When the Lok Sabha transmits Finance Bill to the Rajya Sabha, it can amend or reject the Bill.
2. When the Lok Sabha transmits Money Bill to the Rajya Sabha, it cannot amend or reject the Bill, it can only make recommendations.
3. In the case of disagreement between the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, there is no joint sitting for Money Bill, but a joint sitting becomes necessary for Finance Bill.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: The Rajya Sabha can amend or reject an ordinary Finance Bill but can only recommend changes to a Money Bill. A joint sitting is possible for a Finance Bill but not 'necessary', so 3 is wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q37

questions.q:
Consider the following statements: Once the Central Government notifies an area as a ‘Community Reserve’
1. the Chief Wildlife Warden of the State becomes the governing authority of such forest
2. hunting is not allowed in such area
3. people of such area are allowed to collect non-timber forest produce
4. people of such area are allowed traditional agricultural practices
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Hunting is banned in Community Reserves and people can collect non-timber forest produce. They are managed by a Community Reserve committee, not the Chief Wildlife Warden.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q38

questions.q:
With reference to ‘Scheduled Areas’ in India, consider the following statements:
1. Within a State, the notification of an area as Scheduled Area takes place through an Order of the President.
2. The largest administrative unit forming the Scheduled Area is the District and the lowest is the cluster of villages in the Block.
3. The Chief Ministers of the concerned States are required to submit annual reports to the Union Home Ministry on the administration of Scheduled Areas in the States.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Scheduled Areas are declared by Presidential Order and range from a district to a cluster of villages. The annual report goes from the Governor to the President, not from the CM to the Home Ministry.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q39

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Supreme Court of India has held in some judgements that the reservation policies made under Article 16(4) of the Constitution of India would be limited by Article 335 for maintenance of efficiency of administration.
Statement-II: Article 335 of the Constitution of India defines the term ‘efficiency of administration’.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The Supreme Court (e.g., M. Nagaraj) has held that Article 335 limits reservation to maintain efficiency. But Article 335 does not define 'efficiency of administration'.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q40

questions.q: In which one of the following regions was Dhanyakataka, which flourished as a prominent Buddhist centre under the Mahasanghikas, located?
questions.e: Dhanyakataka (Amaravati) in the Andhra region was a major Mahasanghika Buddhist centre.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q41

questions.q:
With reference to ancient India, consider the following statements:
1. The concept of Stupa is Buddhist in origin.
2. Stupa was generally a repository of relics.
3. Stupa was a votive and commemorative structure in Buddhist tradition.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Stupas held relics and served as votive and commemorative structures. The practice of building mounds predates Buddhism, so 1 is wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q42

questions.q: With reference to ancient South India, Korkai, Poompuhar and Muchiri were well known as
questions.e: Korkai (Pandya), Poompuhar (Chola) and Muchiri/Muziris (Chera) were major ports.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q43

questions.q: Which one of the following explains the practice of ‘Vattakirutal’ as mentioned in Sangam poems?
o: Learned persons assembling in royal courts to discuss religious and philosophical matters
Young girls keeping watch over agricultural fields and driving away birds and animals
A king defeated in a battle committing ritual suicide by starving himself to death
questions.e: Vadakkiruttal was the Sangam practice of a defeated or disgraced king fasting to death facing north.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q44

questions.q:
Consider the following dynasties:
1. Hoysala
2. Gahadavala
3. Kakatiya
4. Yadava
How many of the above dynasties established their kingdoms in early eighth century AD?
questions.e: Hoysalas, Gahadavalas, Kakatiyas and Yadavas all rose in the 11th-12th centuries, not the early 8th.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q45

questions.q:
With reference to ancient Indian History, consider the following pairs: Literary work Author
1. Devichandragupta Bilhana
2. Hammira-Mahakavya Nayachandra Suri
3. Milinda-panha Nagarjuna
4. Nitivakyamrita Somadeva Suri
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Hammira-Mahakavya is by Nayachandra Suri and Nitivakyamrita by Somadeva Suri. Devichandragupta is by Vishakhadatta and Milinda-panha centres on Nagasena.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q46

questions.q: "Souls are not only the property of animal and plant life, but also of rocks, running water and many other natural objects not looked on as living by other religious sects." The above statement reflects one of the core beliefs of which one of the following religious sects of ancient India?
questions.e: Jainism holds that even stones, rocks and water have life (jiva), which underlies its strict ahimsa.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q47

questions.q: Who among the following rulers of Vijayanagara Empire constructed a large dam across Tungabhadra River and a canal-cum-aqueduct several kilometres long from the river to the capital city?
questions.e: Devaraya I built a dam across the Tungabhadra and a long aqueduct to the capital.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q48

questions.q: Who among the following rulers of medieval Gujarat surrendered Diu to Portuguese?
questions.e: Bahadur Shah of Gujarat allowed the Portuguese to build a fort at Diu by a 1535 treaty.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q49

questions.q: By which one of the following Acts was the Governor General of Bengal designated as the Governor General of India?
questions.e: The Charter Act of 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q50

questions.q:
Consider the following statements in relation to Janani Suraksha Yojana:
1. It is a safe motherhood intervention of the State Health Departments.
2. Its objective is to reduce maternal and neonatal mortality among poor pregnant women.
3. It aims to promote institutional delivery among poor pregnant women.
4. Its objective includes providing public health facilities to sick infants up to one year of age.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Janani Suraksha Yojana aims to cut maternal and neonatal deaths by promoting institutional delivery among poor women. It is a central scheme under NHM and does not cover sick infants.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q51

questions.q:
Consider the following statements in the context of interventions being undertaken under Anaemia Mukt Bharat Strategy:
1. It provides prophylactic calcium supplementation for pre-school children, adolescents and pregnant women.
2. It runs a campaign for delayed cord clamping at the time of childbirth.
3. It provides for periodic deworming to children and adolescents.
4. It addresses non-nutritional causes of anaemia in endemic pockets with special focus on malaria, hemoglobinopathies and fluorosis.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Anaemia Mukt Bharat promotes delayed cord clamping, deworming and tackling non-nutritional causes. It gives iron-folic acid, not calcium.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q52

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Carbon fibres are used in the manufacture of components used in automobiles and aircrafts.
2. Carbon fibres once used cannot be recycled.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Carbon fibre is used in automobile and aircraft parts, and it can be recovered and recycled.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q53

questions.q:
Consider the following actions:
1. Detection of car crash/collision which results in the deployment of airbags almost instantaneously
2. Detection of accidental free fall of a laptop towards the ground which results in the immediate turning off of the hard drive
3. Detection of the tilt of the smartphone which results in the rotation of display between portrait and landscape mode In how many of the above actions is the function of accelerometer required?
questions.e: Airbag deployment, laptop free-fall protection and screen rotation all rely on accelerometers.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q54

questions.q:
With reference to the role of biofilters in Recirculating Aquaculture System, consider the following statements:
1. Biofilters provide waste treatment by removing uneaten fish feed.
2. Biofilters convert ammonia present in fish waste to nitrate.
3. Biofilters increase phosphorus as nutrient for fish in water.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: In recirculating aquaculture, biofilters treat waste and convert toxic ammonia to nitrate. They do not add phosphorus.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q55

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs: Objects in space Description
1. Cepheids Giant clouds of dust and gas in space
2. Nebulae Stars which brighten and dim periodically
3. Pulsars Neutron stars that are formed when massive stars run out of fuel and collapse
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Cepheids are pulsating variable stars and nebulae are dust and gas clouds, so pairs 1 and 2 are swapped. Pulsars are collapsed neutron stars.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q56

questions.q: Which one of the following countries has its own Satellite Navigation System?
questions.e: Japan runs its own regional satellite navigation system, QZSS (Michibiki).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q57

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ballistic missiles are jet-propelled at subsonic speeds throughout their flights, while cruise missiles are rocket- powered only in the initial phase of flight.
2. Agni-V is a medium-range supersonic cruise missile, while BrahMos is a solid-fuelled intercontinental ballistic missile.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Ballistic missiles are rocket-boosted then follow an arc, while cruise missiles fly under jet power. Agni-V is an ICBM and BrahMos a cruise missile. Both statements are reversed.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q58

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding mercury pollution:
1. Gold mining activity is a source of mercury pollution in the world.
2. Coal-based thermal power plants cause mercury pollution.
3. There is no known safe level of exposure to mercury.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Gold mining and coal power plants are major mercury sources. Tolerable intake levels exist, so 3 is wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q59

questions.q:
With reference to green hydrogen, consider the following statements:
1. It can be used directly as a fuel for internal combustion.
2. It can be blended with natural gas and used as fuel for heat or power generation.
3. It can be used in the hydrogen fuel cell to run vehicles.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Green hydrogen can burn in engines, be blended into natural gas, and power fuel cells. All three are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q60

questions.q:
Consider the following countries:
1. Bulgaria
2. Czech Republic
3. Hungary
4. Latvia
5. Lithuania
6. Romania
How many of the above-mentioned countries share a land border with Ukraine?
questions.e: Of these, only Hungary and Romania border Ukraine.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q61

questions.q: With reference to the Earth's atmosphere, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: The total amount of insolation received at the equator is roughly about 10 times of that received at the poles.
Infrared rays constitute roughly two-thirds of insolation.
Infrared waves are largely absorbed by water vapour that is concentrated in the lower atmosphere.
Infrared waves are a part of visible spectrum of electromagnetic waves of solar radiation.
questions.e: Water vapour in the lower atmosphere absorbs much infrared radiation. Infrared is not visible light, and the other options misstate insolation.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q62

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The soil in tropical rain forests is rich in nutrients.
Statement-II: The high temperature and moisture of tropical rain forests cause dead organic matter in the soil to decompose quickly.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Heat and moisture make organic matter decompose fast, and heavy rain leaches nutrients, so rainforest soils are poor. Statement-I is wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q63

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The temperature contrast between continents and oceans is greater during summer than in winter.
Statement-II: The specific heat of water is more than that of land surface.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Land-ocean temperature contrast is greater in winter. Water's higher specific heat (Statement-II) is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q64

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In a seismograph, P waves are recorded earlier than S waves.
2. In P waves, the individual particles vibrate to and fro in the direction of wave propagation whereas in S waves, the particles vibrate up and down at right angles to the direction of wave propagation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: P waves are faster and recorded first, and vibrate along the direction of travel; S waves vibrate at right angles. Both are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q65

questions.q:
With reference to coal-based thermal power plants in India, consider the following statements:
1. None of them uses seawater.
2. None of them is set up in water-stressed district.
3. None of them is privately owned.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Some coal plants (like Mundra) use seawater, many are in water-stressed districts, and many are private. None is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q66

questions.q: 'Wolbachia method' is sometimes talked about with reference to which one of the following?
o: Controlling the viral diseases spread by mosquitoes
Converting crop residues into packing material
Producing biochar from thermochemical conversion of biomass
questions.e: Mosquitoes carrying Wolbachia bacteria transmit dengue and similar viruses much less, so it is used to control mosquito-borne viral diseases.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q67

questions.q:
Consider the following activities:
1. Spreading finely ground basalt rock on farmlands extensively
2. Increasing the alkalinity of oceans by adding lime
3. Capturing carbon dioxide released by various industries and pumping it into abandoned subterranean mines in the form of carbonated waters
How many of the above activities are often considered and discussed for carbon capture and sequestration?
questions.e: Spreading crushed basalt, ocean alkalinity enhancement and storing CO₂ in old mines are all discussed for carbon removal.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q68

questions.q: 'Aerial metagenomics' best refers to which one of the following situations?
o: Collecting DNA samples from air in a habitat at one go
Understanding the genetic makeup of avian species of a habitat
Using air-borne devices to collect blood samples from moving animals
Sending drones to inaccessible areas to collect plant and animal samples from land surfaces and water bodies
questions.e: Aerial metagenomics collects DNA from air in a habitat to identify the organisms present.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q69

questions.q: 'Microsatellite DNA' is used in the case of which one of the following?
o: Studying the evolutionary relationships among various species of fauna
Stimulating 'stem cells' to transform into diverse functional tissues
Promoting clonal propagation of horticultural plants
Assessing the efficacy of drugs by conducting series of drug trials in a population
questions.e: Microsatellites are short repeated DNA sequences that vary between individuals; they help study genetic and evolutionary relationships.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q70

questions.q:
Consider the following statements with reference to India:
1. According to the 'Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act, 2006', the 'medium enterprises' are those with investments in plant and machinery between ₹15 crore and ₹25 crore.
2. All bank loans to the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises qualify under the priority sector.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: All bank loans to MSMEs count as priority sector lending. The medium enterprise limit is not ₹15-25 crore.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q71

questions.q:
With reference to Central Bank digital currencies, consider the following statements:
1. It is possible to make payments in a digital currency without using US dollar or SWIFT system.
2. A digital currency can be distributed with a condition programmed into it such as a time-frame for spending it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: A CBDC can move between parties without dollars or SWIFT, and it can be programmed with conditions like an expiry date. Both are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q72

questions.q: In the context of finance, the term ‘beta’ refers to
o: the process of simultaneous buying and selling of an asset from different platforms
an investment strategy of a portfolio manager to balance risk versus reward
a type of systemic risk that arises where perfect hedging is not possible
a numeric value that measures the fluctuations of a stock to changes in the overall stock market
questions.e: Beta measures how much a stock tends to move relative to the overall market.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q73

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Self-Help Group (SHG) programme was originally initiated by the State Bank of India by providing microcredit to the financially deprived.
2. In an SHG, all members of a group take responsibility for a loan that an individual member takes.
3. The Regional Rural Banks and Scheduled Commercial Banks support SHGs.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: In an SHG the group stands behind each member's loan, and RRBs and commercial banks lend to SHGs. The SHG-bank linkage was started by NABARD, not SBI.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q74

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: India's public sector health care system largely focuses on curative care with limited preventive, promotive and rehabilitative care.
Statement-II: Under India's decentralized approach to health care delivery, the States are primarily responsible for organizing health services.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Public health care in India is largely curative, and States organise health services. Both are true, but the second does not explain the first.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q75

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: According to the United Nations' 'World Water Development Report, 2022', India extracts more than a quarter of the world's groundwater withdrawal each year.
Statement-II: India needs to extract more than a quarter of the world's groundwater each year to satisfy the drinking water and sanitation needs of almost 18% of world's population living in its territory.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: India extracts over a quarter of the world's groundwater, but most goes to irrigation, not drinking water and sanitation.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q76

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. According to the Constitution of India, the Central Government has a duty to protect States from internal disturbances.
2. The Constitution of India exempts the States from providing legal counsel to a person being held for preventive detention.
3. According to the Prevention of Terrorism Act, 2002, confession of the accused before the police cannot be used as evidence.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Article 355 makes the Union protect States from internal disturbance, and Article 22 denies preventive detainees the right to counsel. POTA made confessions to senior police officers admissible.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q77

questions.q: Which one of the following countries has been suffering from decades of civil strife and food shortages and was in news in the recent past for its very severe famine?
questions.e: Somalia, after decades of conflict and a prolonged drought, faced severe famine warnings in 2022.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q78

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In India, the Biodiversity Management Committees are key to the realization of the objectives of the Nagoya Protocol.
2. The Biodiversity Management Committees have important functions in determining access and benefit sharing, including the power to levy collection fees on the access of biological resources within its jurisdiction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Biodiversity Management Committees implement access and benefit sharing under the Biological Diversity Act, including levying collection fees, which serves the Nagoya Protocol.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q79

questions.q:
Consider the following statements in respect of election to the President of India:
1. The members nominated to either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assemblies of States are also eligible to be included in the Electoral College.
2. Higher the number of elective Assembly seats, higher is the value of vote of each MLA of that State.
3. The value of vote of each MLA of Madhya Pradesh is greater than that of Kerala.
4. The value of vote of each MLA of Puducherry is higher than that of Arunachal Pradesh because the ratio of total population to total number of elective seats in Puducherry is greater as compared to Arunachal Pradesh.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only elected members form the Electoral College, and more seats lower each MLA's vote value. Puducherry's higher population per seat gives its MLAs a higher value than Arunachal's, so only 4 is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q80

questions.q: With reference to the Indian History, Alexander Rea, A. H. Longhurst, Robert Sewell, James Burgess and Walter Elliot were associated with
o: establishment of English Press in Colonial India
establishment of Churches in Princely States
construction of railways in Colonial India
questions.e: Rea, Longhurst, Sewell, Burgess and Elliot were colonial-era archaeologists and antiquarians.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q81

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs: Site Well known for
1. Besnagar Shaivite cave shrine
2. Bhaja Buddhist cave shrine
3. Sittanavasal Jain cave shrine
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Bhaja has Buddhist caves and Sittanavasal Jain caves. Besnagar is known for the Heliodorus (Vaishnava) pillar.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q82

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: 7th August is declared as the National Handloom Day.
Statement-II: It was in 1905 that the Swadeshi Movement was launched on the same day.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: National Handloom Day is 7 August because the Swadeshi Movement was launched on 7 August 1905. Statement-II explains Statement-I.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q83

questions.q:
Consider the following statements in respect of the National Flag of India according to the Flag Code of India, 2002:
Statement-I: One of the standard sizes of the National Flag of India is 600 mm × 400 mm.
Statement-II: The ratio of the length to the height (width) of the Flag shall be 3:2.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The Flag Code fixes the ratio at 3:2, but 600 × 400 mm is not among the nine standard sizes.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q84

questions.q:
Consider the following statements in respect of the Constitution Day:
Statement-I: The Constitution Day is celebrated on 26th November every year to promote constitutional values among citizens.
Statement-II: On 26th November, 1949, the Constituent Assembly of India set up a Drafting Committee under the Chairmanship of Dr. B. R. Ambedkar to prepare a Draft Constitution of India.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Constitution Day on 26 November marks the adoption of the Constitution in 1949. The Drafting Committee was set up on 29 August 1947.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q85

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Switzerland is one of the leading exporters of gold in terms of value.
Statement-II: Switzerland has the second largest gold reserves in the world.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Switzerland is a leading gold refining and exporting hub, but its reserves are far below the US and Germany.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q86

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Recently, the United States of America (USA) and the European Union (EU) have launched the ‘Trade and Technology Council’.
Statement-II: The USA and the EU claim that through this they are trying to bring technological progress and physical productivity under their control.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The US-EU Trade and Technology Council was launched in 2021 to coordinate on trade and technology, not to control technological progress.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q87

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: India accounts for 3.2% of global export of goods.
Statement-II: Many local companies and some foreign companies operating in India have taken advantage of India's 'Production-linked Incentive' scheme.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: India's share of world goods exports was about 1.8%, not 3.2%. Many Indian and foreign firms have used the PLI schemes.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q88

questions.q:
Consider the following statements: The 'Stability and Growth Pact' of the European Union is a treaty that
1. limits the levels of the budgetary deficit of the countries of the European Union
2. makes the countries of the European Union to share their infrastructure facilities
3. enables the countries of the European Union to share their technologies
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: The EU's Stability and Growth Pact limits budget deficits (3% of GDP) and debt. It says nothing about sharing infrastructure or technology.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q89

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Recently, all the countries of the United Nations have adopted the first-ever compact for international migration, the 'Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration (GCM)'.
2. The objectives and commitments stated in the GCM are binding on the UN member countries.
3. The GCM addresses internal migration or internally displaced people also in its objectives and commitments.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: The Global Compact for Migration was endorsed by vote, not by all members, is non-binding, and covers only international migration. None is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q90

questions.q:
With reference to Home Guards, consider the following statements:
1. Home Guards are raised under the Home Guards Act and Rules of the Central Government.
2. The role of the Home Guards is to serve as an auxiliary force to the police in maintenance of internal security.
3. To prevent infiltration on the international border/coastal areas, the Border Wing Home Guards Battalions have been raised in some States.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Home Guards are auxiliary to the police, and Border Wing battalions guard borders in some states. They are raised under State, not Central, Acts.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q91
questions.u: Justice Administration, Law Enforcement & Statutory Frameworks

questions.q:
With reference to India, consider the following pairs: Action The Act under which it is covered
1. Unauthorized wearing of police or military uniforms The Official Secrets Act, 1923
2. Knowingly misleading or otherwise interfering with a police officer or military officer when engaged in their duties The Indian Evidence Act, 1872
3. Celebratory gunfire which can endanger the personal safety of others The Arms (Amendment) Act, 2019
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Wearing police/military uniforms without authority is covered by the Official Secrets Act, and celebratory gunfire by the Arms (Amendment) Act 2019. Interfering with officers is also under the OSA, not the Evidence Act.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q92
questions.u: Justice Administration, Law Enforcement & Statutory Frameworks

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs: Regions often mentioned in news Reason for being in news
1. North Kivu and Ituri War between Armenia and Azerbaijan
2. Nagorno-Karabakh Insurgency in Mozambique
3. Kherson and Zaporizhzhia Dispute between Israel and Lebanon
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: North Kivu and Ituri are in DR Congo, Nagorno-Karabakh is the Armenia-Azerbaijan dispute, and Kherson and Zaporizhzhia are in Ukraine. None is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q93

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Israel has established diplomatic relations with some Arab States.
Statement-II: The 'Arab Peace Initiative' mediated by Saudi Arabia was signed by Israel and Arab League.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Israel has normalised ties with the UAE, Bahrain and others. The Arab Peace Initiative (2002) was a Saudi proposal adopted by the Arab League; Israel never signed it.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q94

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs with regard to sports awards:
1. Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award — For the most spectacular and outstanding performance by a sportsperson over period of last four years
2. Arjuna Award — For the lifetime achievement by a sportsperson
3. Dronacharya Award — To honour eminent coaches who have successfully trained sportspersons or teams
4. Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puraskar — To recognize the contribution made by sportspersons even after their retirement
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: The Khel Ratna is for outstanding performance over four years and the Dronacharya for coaches. The Arjuna is not for lifetime achievement, and the Khel Protsahan Puraskar goes to organisations.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q95

questions.q:
Consider the following statements in respect of the 44th Chess Olympiad, 2022:
1. It was the first time that Chess Olympiad was held in India.
2. The official mascot was named 'Thambi'.
3. The trophy for the winning team in the open section is the Vera Menchik Cup.
4. The trophy for the winning team in the women's section is the Hamilton-Russell Cup.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 2022 Chennai Olympiad was India's first and its mascot was Thambi. The open-section trophy is the Hamilton-Russell Cup and the women's the Vera Menchik Cup.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q96

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs: Area of conflict mentioned in news Country where it is located
1. Donbas Syria
2. Kachin Ethiopia
3. Tigray North Yemen
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Donbas is in Ukraine, Kachin in Myanmar and Tigray in Ethiopia. None is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q97

questions.q: In the recent years Chad, Guinea, Mali and Sudan caught the international attention for which one of the following reasons common to all of them?
o: Discovery of rich deposits of rare earth elements
questions.e: Chad, Guinea, Mali and Sudan all saw military coups in 2020-21.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q98

questions.q:
Consider the following heavy industries:
1. Fertilizer plants
2. Oil refineries
3. Steel plants Green hydrogen is expected to play a significant role in decarbonizing how many of the above industries?
questions.e: Green hydrogen can replace fossil hydrogen in fertiliser plants and refineries, and coal in steel making. All three.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q99

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about G-20:
1. The G-20 group was originally established as a platform for the Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors to discuss the international economic and financial issues.
2. Digital public infrastructure is one of India's G-20 priorities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The G20 began in 1999 as a forum of finance ministers and central bank governors, and digital public infrastructure was an Indian G20 priority in 2023.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2023, GS Paper I, Q100
